title: Implement trellis MVP — agentic-readiness audit & sync per SPEC.md
description: Parent seed for the trellis MVP build-out. SPEC.md (repo root) is the design record: a mostly-deterministic, partly-agentic audit tool that scores repos 0-100% against a versioned 90-criterion rubric (9 categories, repo-scope + app-scope), maps to maturity Levels 1-5 with a coverage-aware clamp, detects canonical-config drift against a bundled standards/ set, and tracks fleet history in central SQLite. Deterministic detectors for TypeScript/Swift/Python; 4 bounded Pi-RPC investigation areas feed a deterministic grader. The plan also carries the os-eco repo standards: warren-stack scaffold (Bun + TS strict + Biome + zod + commander + pino), L5 toolkit ratchets + check:all, .github governance + CI/publish workflows, .claude/commands, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/RUNBOOK and the rest of the standard root files.

title: Scaffold the repo: Bun + TS-strict skeleton, os-eco baseline configs, package.json (@os-eco/trellis-cli, bin trellis), src/ tree per SPEC §4

DELIVERABLES (declarative end state): package.json exists with name @os-eco/trellis-cli, version 0.0.1, type module, bin { "trellis": "./src/cli/main.ts" }, engines.bun >= 1.1.0, author/license/repository fields matching the warren/seeds pattern; devDependencies include @biomejs/biome, @types/bun, typescript, knip; dependencies include commander, zod, pino, js-yaml (+ @types/js-yaml). src/index.ts exports `export const VERSION = "0.0.1"` (kept in lockstep with package.json — the release workflow asserts this). Baseline configs are copied from templates/l5-toolkit/configs/ and adapted: biome.json (kebab-case filenaming, complexity caps, tab indent / 100-col), tsconfig.base.json + tsconfig.json extending it (strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, no any), bunfig.toml, knip.json, .jscpd.json. .gitignore seeded from templates/l5-toolkit/env/.gitignore.template; .env.example present (investigation env keys: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY etc. documented, values blank); LICENSE is MIT. The src/ directory tree exists per SPEC §4 (cli/, client/, rubric/, discovery/, detectors/{common,lang/typescript,lang/swift,lang/python,oseco}/, investigation/provider/pi/, scoring/, standards/canonical/, fleet/, store/migrations/, report/) with placeholder index modules so typecheck passes. targets.yaml.example exists per SPEC §6.5. Package scripts: test, lint (biome check --error-on-warnings .), lint:fix, typecheck (tsc --noEmit). ACCEPTANCE: bun install && bun test && bun run lint && bun run typecheck all exit 0; `bun run src/cli/main.ts --help` prints a stub. Conventions: .ts import extensions, tests <name>.test.ts beside the unit. REFERENCES: SPEC §4, §13; warren/package.json; templates/l5-toolkit/configs/.

title: Rubric schema + loader: zod schemas for criterion/category records, RUBRIC_VERSION + comparability policy, load-time invariants (SPEC §6.1)
description: Implement the rubric schema and loader — the WHAT layer that never names a tool. DELIVERABLES: src/rubric/schema.ts defines zod schemas for category records ({ id: snake_case, title, description }) and criterion records ({ id, category, scope: repo|app, level: 1-5, skippable: boolean, discoveryVia: deterministic|agent, investigation: documentation|agent-config|setup-runnability|test-layout|null, gate: boolean (reserved), weight: positive number default 1 (reserved) }) per SPEC §6.1. src/rubric/version.ts exports RUBRIC_VERSION = "0.2.0" plus a comment block recording the semver-by-comparability policy (major = moves scores for unchanged code; minor = additive; patch = wording; pre-1.0 comparability changes ride minor) per SPEC §3.5. A loader function parses categories.yaml / repo-scope.yaml / app-scope.yaml and enforces load-time invariants: investigation non-null IFF discoveryVia=agent; exactly one gate:true per category; weight > 0; every entry's scope matches its source file; category references resolve; ids unique. Violations throw with the offending id and file. DELIVERABLE TESTS: schema round-trip, each invariant violated in a fixture and rejected with a precise error. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; loader exported from the rubric core module (no CLI yet). REFERENCES: SPEC §3.1-3.5, §6.1.

title: Scoring engine: per-criterion score, pass rate, coverage clamp, naKind handling, 20-pt bands, repo/app aggregation — pure functions unit-tested against §3.4 worked examples
description: Implement the scoring engine as pure, surface-agnostic core functions. DELIVERABLES: src/scoring/ exports functions implementing SPEC §3.4 exactly: perCriterionScore = numerator/denominator with null (N/A) excluded; passRate = mean over counted criteria; coverage = counted / (counted + no-detector + skipped); band() mapping 20-pt bands (L1 0-20 … L5 80-100); level = min(passRateLevel, coverageLevel) — the clamp is monotonic, only ever lowers. naKind discipline: not-applicable excluded from the coverage base, no-detector counted against coverage. Repo/app aggregation: app-scope criteria roll N per-app DetectorResults into numerator=passing-apps / denominator=N; repo-scope denominator always 1. gate/weight fields are read into types but NOT consulted by the v0 scorer (reserved per SPEC §3.3). DELIVERABLE TESTS: worked examples covering every band boundary, clamp no-op at full coverage, clamp lowering on thin coverage, both naKind paths, multi-app aggregation, and the §6.2 scorecard-entry shape (numerator/denominator/rationale ≤500 chars/naKind). ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; functions are pure (no I/O). REFERENCES: SPEC §3.2-3.4, §6.2.

title: Detector infrastructure: DetectionContext + DetectorResult contract (SPEC §8.1), criterion→detector registry, not-applicable vs no-detector discipline
description: Build the deterministic detector infrastructure. DELIVERABLES: src/detectors/ exports the SPEC §8.1 contract verbatim: DetectionContext { repoPath, app: { path, languages }, run(argv, opts), readFile(rel), glob(pattern) } and DetectorResult { numerator: number|null, denominator: 1, naKind?, rationale ≤500 chars }; type Detector = (ctx) => Promise<DetectorResult>. src/detectors/registry.ts binds criterion id → detector with per-language adapter resolution (a criterion may bind common, per-language, or be unbound); an unbound deterministic criterion resolves to no-detector with a clear rationale — never a crash, never a false pass. The run() helper executes subprocesses sandboxed to the target repo cwd with timeouts and captures exit/stdout/stderr; nothing in any detector may write to the target repo (read-only mandate). Discipline encoded as helpers: notApplicable(reason) for honestly-absent surfaces vs noDetector(reason) for should-have-measured-but-couldn't (tool missing, ambiguous evidence). DELIVERABLE TESTS: registry resolution precedence, unbound-criterion fallback, run() timeout/error mapping, both helper paths. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; registry covers all 70 deterministic criterion ids (bound or explicit no-detector stub). REFERENCES: SPEC §8.1, §3.2.

title: App discovery (SPEC §8.2): find independently-deployable directories as apps; 0 found → repo root is 1 app; app map recorded in the report

If 0 apps found, the repo root is exactly 1 app. Each discovered app carries { path, languages[] } with language detection (ts/js via tsconfig/package.json, swift via Package.swift, python via pyproject/setup.cfg), honoring the optional `languages` hint from targets.yaml when present. The app map feeds the report's §6.3 `apps` object ({ path: { description } }). DELIVERABLE TESTS: fixture trees for single-app root, multi-app monorepo (warren-like src/ui + server), hint override, and exclusion rules. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; discovery is pure given a filesystem (deterministic ordering — sort by path). REFERENCES: SPEC §8.2, §6.3, §6.5.

title: SQLite store (bun:sqlite): schema.sql + migrations for runs / criterion_results / investigation_cache (SPEC §6.4), audit persistence wired in
description: Implement the central SQLite store. DELIVERABLES: src/store/ uses bun:sqlite with schema.sql + sequential migrations under src/store/migrations/ creating exactly the SPEC §6.4 tables: runs (id, repo, commit_sha, rubric_version, level, pass_rate, coverage, report_json, scored_at; index runs_repo_time), criterion_results (run_id FK, criterion, numerator nullable, denominator, na_kind, rationale; index cr_run), investigation_cache (PK repo+commit_sha+area, findings_json, created_at). A store module exposes typed functions: openStore(dbPath) with migration-on-open, insertRun(report) writing the runs row + exploded criterion_results in one transaction, latestRun(repo), runsSince(repo, date), cache get/put for investigations. DB location: a trellis-owned path (e.g. ~/.trellis/trellis.db) overridable via env/flag — never inside an audited repo (central-state non-goal, SPEC §2). `trellis audit` now persists each run. DELIVERABLE TESTS: migration idempotency, transactional insert, query round-trips against a temp DB. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; two audits of the same fixture produce two runs rows with identical report_json. REFERENCES: SPEC §6.4, §2 (central state), §11.

title: Investigation layer core: the 4 fixed areas (areas.ts), zod findings schemas per area (findings.ts), and the pure deterministic grader (facts → pass/fail/N-A, SPEC §7)
description: Build the investigation core: areas, findings contracts, and the deterministic grader. DELIVERABLES: src/investigation/areas.ts defines the 4 fixed areas (documentation, agent-config, setup-runnability, test-layout) each with id, description, and the per-area investigation prompt scaffold (what facts to gather, read-only, call submit_findings exactly once, facts never verdicts) per SPEC §7.1/§9.2. src/investigation/findings.ts defines one zod schema per area capturing objective facts only (the AgentConfigFindings example in SPEC §7.2 is the shape model — finalize all four: documentation files/freshness/build-cmd/runbooks/arch-docs; agent instruction files + skills + validation automation + co-authorship count; secrets mechanism + scripted services + devcontainer buildability evidence; test dirs/naming/integration boundaries/isolation/timing surfaces). src/investigation/grader.ts is pure and deterministic: for each of the 20 agent criteria, a function from the bound area's Findings (+ skippable rules) to { numerator, denominator, naKind?, rationale } — e.g. agents_md passes iff some instruction file has all four booleans; skills passes iff ≥1 skill has name+description+non-empty prompt. Same facts → same grade, byte-identical rationale. DELIVERABLE TESTS: per-criterion grader tables (facts → expected grade) covering pass/fail/N-A for all 20 agent criteria; schema rejection of verdict-shaped extras. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; all 20 agent criterion ids map to a grader function. REFERENCES: SPEC §7.1-7.2, §5 (agent-tagged rows).

title: Pi RPC provider (SPEC §9): argv builder, findings-extension.ts (submit_findings tool), JSONL event loop, env passthrough, corrective-prompt retries, heartbeat watchdog, version probe + graceful no-detector degradation
description:
Implement the Pi RPC provider — the single transport through which facts are produced. DELIVERABLES: src/investigation/provider/ exposes investigate(repoPath, area, opts): Promise (SPEC §9.0 core entrypoint). buildPiArgv mirrors burrow (../burrow/src/runtime/pi.ts reference): pi --mode rpc --no-session --no-extensions -e --offline --no-context-files --provider

--model --tools ,submit_findings --system-prompt , cwd = target repo. src/investigation/provider/pi/findings-extension.ts registers the submit_findings tool whose parameter JSON-schema derives from the area's zod schema via zod-to-json-schema. Protocol per SPEC §9.3: write one prompt line, HOLD STDIN OPEN, watch stdout JSONL for the submit_findings toolCall, zod-validate arguments, close stdin on capture; on missing/invalid call send one corrective prompt echoing zod errors, bounded to N retries (default 2); exhaustion/timeout/stopReason:error → resolve no-detector with the failure rationale, never a fabricated pass. Heartbeat watchdog force-terminates stalls. Provider/model selection precedence: CLI flags > targets.yaml defaults.investigation > one documented constant; provider names lowercased. Env passthrough only (never argv): ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/AUTH_TOKEN/BASE_URL always + the PI_PROVIDER_ENV_KEYS map (openai/google/groq/mistral/deepseek) per §9.4. Startup probe: pi --version against the documented supported version; missing/incompatible Pi degrades every agent criterion to no-detector with a hint — never crashes the audit. DELIVERABLE TESTS: argv construction, env filtering, retry/corrective flow, watchdog, and degradation — all against a scripted fake pi process (no live calls). ACCEPTANCE: bun test green with zero network/model access. REFERENCES: SPEC §9.0-9.6.

title: Golden fixtures + offline test harness (SPEC §9.7): captured + canonicalized Pi RPC sessions per area under __golden__/, parser → zod → grader exercised fully offline, TRELLIS_UPDATE_PI_GOLDEN regeneration gate
description: Create the golden-fixture suite for the investigation layer. DELIVERABLES: src/investigation/__golden__/ holds one captured real `pi --mode rpc` session per area (full JSONL event stream including the submit_findings toolCall), canonicalized — timestamps, responseId, session/tool-call ids, usage normalized to fixed placeholders — and frozen. A capture/regeneration script (scripts/ or test helper) re-records goldens ONLY when TRELLIS_UPDATE_PI_GOLDEN=1 AND an explicit live-call flag are both set; otherwise it refuses. Unit tests run the full chain offline: RPC parser → toolCall capture → zod validation → deterministic grader, asserting the exact grades each golden produces; a corrupted-golden fixture exercises the corrective/no-detector path. CI configuration makes no model calls anywhere (assert via test that no network env is required). ACCEPTANCE: bun test green offline with PI/API env vars unset; regeneration script documented in AGENTS.md/RUNBOOK; goldens stable across two consecutive test runs. NOTE: the initial capture requires one live Pi run per area by the operator — coordinate with the user if no capture exists yet; until then hand-authored fixtures matching the real wire shape (validated against burrow's documented v0.74.0 envelope) are acceptable and marked as such. REFERENCES: SPEC §9.7, burrow golden methodology.

title: Wire investigation into audit: investigate() core entrypoint, investigation_cache keyed (repo, commit_sha, area), --no-cache flag, agent criteria flow into the scorecard
description: Wire the investigation layer into the audit pipeline with caching. DELIVERABLES: the audit core, for each of the 4 areas referenced by any to-be-scored agent criterion, resolves findings via: investigation_cache lookup keyed (repo, commit_sha, area) → on miss, investigate() (Pi provider) → zod-validate → cache write; --no-cache forces re-investigation (SPEC §7.3/§9.5). Grader output for all 20 agent criteria flows into the scorecard alongside deterministic results; rationale strings name the area + key facts. Areas run once per repo per commit regardless of how many criteria consume them (bounded LLM cost). Pi-unavailable or area-failure paths surface as no-detector entries counted against coverage. commit_sha resolution: git rev-parse HEAD of the target; dirty worktrees recorded with a -dirty suffix so cache keys never lie. DELIVERABLE TESTS: cache hit/miss/no-cache flows against a temp DB with a stubbed provider; an end-to-end audit of a fixture repo where agent criteria score from cached findings, asserting byte-identical scorecards across two runs at the same commit. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; `trellis audit` on a fixture exercises det + agent criteria together; re-run at same commit is byte-identical. REFERENCES: SPEC §7.3, §9.5, §3.2.

title: Canonical standards set: src/standards/canonical/ files extracted from the l5-toolkit/warren conventions + manifest.yaml with per-file semver, hashes, and matcher kinds (SPEC §10)
description: Author the canonical standards set and manifest. DELIVERABLES: src/standards/canonical/ contains the bundled canonical files per SPEC §10, extracted from the current os-eco conventions (templates/l5-toolkit + warren as reference): biome.json, tsconfig.base.json, .github/workflows/ci.yml, AGENTS.md (template/section-aware), scripts/hooks/pre-commit, .seeds/config.yaml — plus any additional files the l5-toolkit treats as canonical (knip.json, .jscpd.json, bunfig.toml, dependabot.yml) where stable. src/standards/manifest.yaml describes the set: top-level version (start "1.0.0"), and per file { path, version, hash: sha256, matcher: exact|json-subset|yaml-subset|text|template }. A small script or test recomputes hashes so manifest drift inside trellis itself fails CI. DELIVERABLE TESTS: manifest schema validation (zod), hash agreement between manifest.yaml and the canonical files on disk, matcher kind coverage. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; `trellis standards` (landing next step) will read this manifest; every canonical file is byte-tracked. REFERENCES: SPEC §10, templates/l5-toolkit/configs+github, warren root configs.

title: Drift engine: drift.ts matchers (exact/json-subset/yaml-subset/text/template), allowed-deltas, per-file states (match/allowed-delta/drift/missing/extra), trellis drift + trellis standards commands, report.drift
description: Implement the drift engine and its CLI commands. DELIVERABLES: src/standards/drift.ts compares a target repo against the canonical set: per-file matchers exact (byte), json-subset (canonical keys must be present/equal, target may extend), yaml-subset, text (normalized whitespace), template (section-aware for AGENTS.md — required sections present, boilerplate matched); per-file output state match | allowed-delta | drift | missing | extra. Allowed deltas honor the targets.yaml shape (file-level and structural paths within a file, each with a reason) — whitelisted divergences report allowed-delta, not drift. The target's tracked canonical version resolves per-repo override > defaults.canonicalVersion. `trellis drift <repo-path>` runs drift standalone (accepts --canonical <v>; without fleet context allowedDeltas default empty); `trellis standards` prints the canonical manifest + versions. Drift results fold into the audit report under report.drift (SPEC §6.3). DELIVERABLE TESTS: fixture repos per matcher kind and per state (match/allowed/drift/missing/extra), structural-path allow-listing, version override resolution. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; `trellis drift` on a warren-stack checkout produces a coherent per-file table in terminal/JSON/MD. REFERENCES: SPEC §10, §6.5, §12.

title: Fleet: targets.yaml loader (defaults, per-target canonical overrides + allowedDeltas, skip, osecoDetectors, languages) + trellis fleet multi-repo orchestration
description: Implement fleet orchestration. DELIVERABLES: src/fleet/ loads and zod-validates targets.yaml per SPEC §6.5: defaults { canonicalVersion, investigation.{provider,model} } and targets[] { id, path, languages?, canonical?: { version?, allowedDeltas? }, skip?: criterion ids forced to not-applicable, osecoDetectors?: boolean }. Path resolution relative to the targets.yaml location; missing/unreadable target paths fail that target with a clear per-target error without aborting the fleet. `trellis fleet [--targets targets.yaml] [--json|--md]` audits every target sequentially (audit + drift with the target's allowedDeltas and skip list applied), persists each run to the central store, and renders an aggregate dashboard: per-repo level, pass rate, coverage, drift counts, and level deltas vs each repo's previous run. The skip list maps to not-applicable with rationale 'skipped via targets.yaml'. DELIVERABLE TESTS: targets schema validation fixtures, skip/osecoDetectors/allowedDeltas plumbing into the audit context, partial-failure isolation, aggregate rendering snapshot. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; a two-fixture-target fleet run writes two runs rows and prints the aggregate table. REFERENCES: SPEC §6.5, §12, §14.7.

title: History reporting: trellis report dashboard from SQLite (--repo/--since/--json/--md) + changes-since-last-run deltas with rubric-version attribution (SPEC §11)
description: Implement history reporting and change attribution. DELIVERABLES: `trellis report [--repo <id>] [--since <date>] [--json|--md]` renders from the central SQLite store: per-repo run history (level, pass rate, coverage over time), fleet snapshot of latest runs, and per-criterion trend queries powered by criterion_results. changesSinceLastRun (SPEC §11): comparing a run against the most recent prior run for the same repo, list per-criterion transitions (pass→fail, fail→pass, naKind changes, app-count/denominator changes) and the net level move; embed in the §6.3 report at audit time and render in `trellis report`. Rubric attribution: when the two runs' rubric_version differ, the delta is flagged explicitly as possibly-rubric-driven; identical versions mark it a real code regression/improvement. DELIVERABLE TESTS: seeded multi-run temp DBs asserting delta computation across all transition kinds, the rubric-version flag both ways, --since filtering, and renderer snapshots. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; after two fleet runs of a changed fixture, `trellis report` shows the criterion-level diff with correct attribution. REFERENCES: SPEC §11, §6.3, §6.4, §12.

title: os-eco-native detectors (SPEC §8.4): seeds/mulch/canopy/plot/skills/check:all/ratchet evidence mapped onto existing criteria, osecoDetectors per-target toggle
description: Implement the os-eco-native detector pack in src/detectors/oseco/. DELIVERABLES: evidence detectors that strengthen EXISTING criteria (no new category, SPEC §8.4), active by default and disabled when the target sets osecoDetectors: false: AGENTS.md+CLAUDE.md richness → agents_md; */SKILL.md → skills; .seeds/ presence + labeling config (+ sd data when available) → issue_templates / issue_labeling_system / backlog_health; check:all script + CI invoking it verbatim → unit_tests_runnable / pre_commit_hooks / fast_ci_feedback evidence; ratchet scripts (file-size/debt/coverage/complexity/bundle/jscpd/knip) → large_file_detection / tech_debt_tracking / code_quality_metrics / dead_code_detection / duplicate_code_detection / unused_dependencies_detection / heavy_dependency_detection; gen:openapi + docs/openapi.yaml → api_schema_docs; gen:docs → automated_doc_generation; .canopy/ → automated_doc_generation evidence; .mulch/ → documentation_freshness / agentic_development; .plot/ → agentic_development; agent co-author trailers in git log → agentic_development. Composition rule: oseco evidence merges with (never replaces) the common/language detector verdicts — pass if either passes; rationale names the oseco evidence path. DELIVERABLE TESTS: fixture repos with/without each surface, the toggle, and merge semantics. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; auditing a warren-stack fixture with the pack on measurably raises honest pass rates vs off. REFERENCES: SPEC §8.4, §6.5.

title: Typed SDK (src/client/) mirroring core types + CLI exit-code contract (--fail-on level|gate|drift|none) so trellis is CI-usable per repo (SPEC §12, §13.1)
description: Ship the typed SDK and the CI-usable exit-code contract. DELIVERABLES: src/client/ exports a typed programmatic client (SPEC §13.1): audit(repoPath, opts), drift(repoPath, opts), fleet(targetsPath, opts), report(query), rubric() — each calling the SAME core functions the CLI does, in-process, with request/response types that mirror the core's exported types (annotated // Mirrors src/<x>). No logic in the SDK beyond type shaping. Exit-code contract across all CLI commands (SPEC §12): 0 clean; non-zero when a gate criterion fails or drift is detected, tunable via --fail-on level|gate|drift|none (document the default; level compares against a --min-level threshold). Sync enforcement: golden snapshots of the stable output shapes (report JSON, drift JSON) live in tests so surface drift turns CI red; strict tsc over the mirrored types. DELIVERABLE TESTS: SDK and CLI invocations of the same audit produce deep-equal reports (one code path proof); each --fail-on mode's exit code asserted via spawned CLI on fixtures. ACCEPTANCE: bun test + check:all green; README/AGENTS.md document the SDK entrypoints and exit codes. REFERENCES: SPEC §12, §13.1.

title: Dogfood gate: trellis audits itself (must band L4+) and the warren-stack fleet end-to-end; iterate detector bindings on what actually mattered
description: Run the dogfood gate. DELIVERABLES: a real targets.yaml at the operator's machine paths covering trellis itself + the warren-stack repos (warren, burrow, plot, mulch, seeds, canopy, sapling); `trellis fleet` completes end-to-end (deterministic + cached investigation criteria + drift + oseco pack); `trellis audit .` on trellis itself bands L4 or higher — if it doesn't, file and fix the honest gaps in trellis's own repo standards (this step includes that remediation) or fix dishonest detectors. Iterate detector bindings on what the fleet run teaches: every no-detector result is triaged into (a) detector bug → fix, (b) genuinely missing adapter → leave counted, or (c) honestly absent surface → reclassify not-applicable; record decisions via ml record. Two consecutive fleet runs at unchanged commits must be byte-identical per repo (determinism check at fleet scale). DELIVERABLES (artifacts): the triage notes land as seeds issues or mulch records; detector fixes land as commits with tests. ACCEPTANCE: trellis self-audit ≥ L4; fleet dashboard renders all targets; check:all green; the SPEC §14 dogfood gate is closed. REFERENCES: SPEC §13 (dogfood mandate), §14 (gate).

title: Release v0.1.0: CHANGELOG roll, version sync (package.json + src VERSION), publish @os-eco/trellis-cli via the version-gated workflow
description: Cut the v0.1.0 release. DELIVERABLES: execute .claude/commands/release.md — review git log since repo birth, bump package.json version AND src/index.ts VERSION to 0.1.0 (the publish workflow fails on mismatch), roll CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] into a dated 0.1.0 section summarizing the MVP surface (audit/drift/fleet/report/rubric/standards commands, 3 language adapters, Pi investigation layer, canonical drift, SQLite history), refresh README/CLAUDE.md stats if command counts changed, commit. Verify the publish path: workflows/publish.yml is version-gated against npm view @os-eco/trellis-cli (package not yet on npm → publishes on first main push once NPM_TOKEN is configured; coordinate with the operator for the token — see ../scripts/set-npm-token.sh at the os-eco root). Final gate: bun test, bun run lint, bun run typecheck, bun run check:all all exit 0; sd close completed plan children; ml record release decision; sd sync. ACCEPTANCE: a release commit exists on main with synced versions and rolled changelog; CI green; npm publish succeeds or is verified blocked only on the operator-held token. REFERENCES: .claude/commands/release.md (authored in step 2), seeds/.github/workflows/publish.yml pattern.
